extracted.intended_audience: industrial design applicants, patent agents, and IP practitioners in the Philippines
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and formal requirements for filing, prosecuting, publishing, registering, renewing, opposing, and cancelling industrial design applications and registrations before the IPOPHL (Philippines). Covers required contents, formality examination, representation/drawings, fees, publication/deferment, adverse information, and Director decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of initial application
rubrics_metrics.description: A duly accomplished request containing the name and address of the applicant or, where the applicant is not the designer, a statement indicating the origin of the right to the industrial design, and an indication of the kind of article of manufacture to which the design shall be applied; a description containing title, applicant name, brief description of views, statement of characteristic feature (if any), and a claim; drawings of different views showing the complete appearance including the applicant's signature; payment of required fees at filing; appointment of agent if applicant is not a resident of the Philippines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific elements (request, description items 1–5, drawings, fees, agent appointment) that must be present for an application to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of photographs or other graphic representations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may accept photographs or other adequate graphic representation of the design provided they comply with the requirements regarding drawings of industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs are acceptable as long as they meet the drawing/regulatory requirements (clarity, numbering, paper, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees upon filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be subject to full payment of the filing fee and the publication fee upon filing. Applications claiming priority must also pay priority claim fee at filing as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay required fees in full at filing has specified consequences (see Effect of Non-payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-payment of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be considered bona fide if all required fees are not paid in full upon filing and will be deemed a failed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may retrieve a failed application by filing a formal written request within four months of the mailing date of the notice of failed application; otherwise it will be expunged. Failed applications due to non-payment are not published and may be filed anew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special form and order of description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must contain, in order: (a) Title of the design; (b) Name of Applicant with first name, middle initial, last name (if natural person); (c) Detailed description of the different views/figures of the drawings; (d) Statement of characteristic features, if any; and (e) Claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must follow the prescribed order and include the listed elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the design must technically designate the particular article embodying the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should identify the article (not be decorative or vague).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawing views
rubrics_metrics.description: Every view should be briefly described (e.g., perspective, front, side, top, bottom, back) and given corresponding figure numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each figure number should correspond to a described view to clarify the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristic feature statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A characteristic feature statement may describe the particular novel and ornamental features of the claimed design considered to be dominant, if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement highlights the dominant novel/ornamental features; include if useful or requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim wording and number
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim shall be in formal terms of the ornamental design using the terms: '(specifying name) substantially as shown and described' or '(specifying name) substantially as shown'. More than one claim is neither required nor permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a single claim permitted; use the specified phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation format and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation shall consist of a graphic or photographic reproduction of the design, in black and white or in color. The representation must be a clear representation and the number of views must constitute a complete disclosure of the appearance of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations must fully disclose appearance; insufficient views may be requested by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface shading and color rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate surface shading shall be used to show character or contour of the surfaces; shading shall not be employed to exemplify color. If color is a material feature, colors may be actually reproduced; otherwise a statement naming colors claimed and the principal parts in such colors must be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shading for form/contour only; claim color explicitly when material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph submission conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs in lieu of formal drawings are permitted provided photographs are printed on prescribed paper, figure numbers shown in black ink proximate to corresponding photograph, and photographs afford a clear view of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paper/numbering/clarity requirements when submitting photos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic/photographic representation requirements (CAD, photos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer-aided drawings (CAD) or clear photographs may be accepted provided they conform to the Regulations, particularly the special requirements for drawings of an industrial design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAD files/photos must meet the same formal drawing requirements (size, clarity, numbering, shading, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of broken lines in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclaimed environmental structure may be shown only in broken lines when necessary; broken lines should not obscure or confuse the claimed design and should not be heavier than lines depicting the claimed design. If broken lines intrude upon the claimed design they should be shown in a separate figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines sparingly and in compliance to avoid confusing the claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple embodiments in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: More than one embodiment of an industrial design in one application may be permissible if the articles are not patentably distinct, have substantially similar dominant design features embodied in a single design concept, and relate to the same class/subclass of the International Classification or same set/composition of articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure embodiments present a single coordinated design concept and classification alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set of articles in one application
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets of articles (items customarily sold or used together) may be the subject of one application if each article has the same or substantially similar design and they constitute a coordinated whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A coordinated whole requirement and similarity test applies for sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require that the application be accompanied by a specimen of the article embodying the industrial design; such requirement shall be subject to payment of prescribed fee within one month from submission of the specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen defined as a sample/unit chosen as typical; fee and timing apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date elements for industrial design
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date shall be the date on which the Office received in English or Filipino: (a) a request indicating registration is sought; (b) description; (c) a single claim; (d) a representation of the article or pictorial representation; (e) payment of required fees at filing; (f) appointment of agent if applicant is non-resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All listed elements must be present to accord a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions regarding 'Incomplete Applications' in Part 6, Rules 600.1 and 600.2 of the Regulations for Patents apply mutatis mutandis to industrial design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete application rules from patent part are applied similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late-filed or missing drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The provision on 'Late-filed or Missing Drawings' in Part 6, Rule 603 of the Regulations for Patents applies mutatis mutandis to industrial design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and time limits for late/missing drawings follow patent rules by analogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration without substantive examination (formal registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: All industrial design applications shall be registered without substantive examination provided all required fees including publication fees are paid and all formal requirements set forth in the Regulations are complied with; provided further the Director does not motu proprio issue a registrability report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is generally formal only, but the Director may exercise authority to assess registrability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's power to issue registrability report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall decide whether to register the industrial design and may issue a registrability report motu proprio. If prior art defeats registrability, the Director may deny registration or direct amendments/additional views; amended applications shall be re-published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though registration is formal, substantive registrability may be examined at Director's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination and evaluation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall conduct a formality examination and report to the applicant. Evaluation considers whether design falls under non-registrable designs; contents of the request; priority documents; proof of authority if applicant not designer; deed of assignment; payment of fees; signatures; identification of designer; contents of description (characteristic feature); and formal drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formality exam checks listed formal and documentary requirements; deficiencies must be addressed by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction or division for multiple designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction or division of multiple design embodiments may be proper if two or more independent or distinct designs are presented in one design application; patent-restriction rules of Part 6 apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple distinct designs are present, a restriction/division may be required; refer to patent rules for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term and renewal of divisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a divisional application (earlier, succeeding, mandatory, or voluntary) shall be five years reckoned from the filing date of the parent application and may be renewed for not more than two consecutive periods of five years each by paying the renewal fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications have a specific 5-year term from parent with limited renewals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of industrial design application
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design application shall be published in the IPOPHL E-Gazette after formality examination prior to registration. The application may be published immediately after filing if description, claim, and drawings comply with Regulations; fees fully paid; priority documents submitted; and other Office requirements complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication timing depends on compliance with formal requirements and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request deferment of publication up to twelve months from filing or priority date; a second period of up to another twelve months may be allowed; a third period is not allowed. Maximum permitted deferment is 24 months from filing/priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request can be made at filing or before publication; if requested after filing the remaining allowed time applies; applicant may request specific publication timing within the allowed maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant actions after formality examination report
rubrics_metrics.description: Within two months from the mailing date of the formality examination report the applicant may amend the application or voluntarily withdraw it. Failure to respond within two months causes withdrawal. Revival of withdrawn application follows Part 9 rules mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month response window; apply patent part procedures for replies, re-exam, final refusal, and revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final action and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant fails to file a complete response to the formality examination report, any subsequent formality examination report shall be a final action which may be appealed to the Director in a manner provided in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final actions may be appealed following appeal procedures in the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary withdrawal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be voluntarily withdrawn by filing a verified declaration of withdrawal and payment of the required fee; the declaration must identify the application and be signed by applicant or assignee of record. A voluntarily withdrawn application shall not be revived and will be deemed forfeited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is final (no revival) except procedures for opposition to withdrawal exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of withdrawal declaration and opposition rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If a declaration of withdrawal is filed it shall be published in the E-Gazette within fifteen days from filing for purposes of opposition. If filed prior to 1st publication, the declaration and application shall not be published and shall not be subject to opposition. Within 15 days from publication any person who believes prejudiced may present a written Opposition with fees in form of a sworn statement substantiated by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition must meet formal requirements or be dismissed; Director resolves opposition; appeals to Director General may be available in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of industrial design registration and renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: The term shall be five years from the filing date and may be renewed for not more than two consecutive periods of five years each by paying the renewal fee (Sections 118.1 and 118.2, IP Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum total term: initial 5 years + up to two renewals of 5 years each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fee timing and grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: The renewal fee shall be paid within twelve months preceding expiration of the registration period. A six-month grace period is allowed for payment after expiration upon payment of a surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay renewal within the 12-month window; late payment allowed during grace with surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for cancellation of design registration
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time during the term any person may petition to cancel the industrial design registration on grounds: (a) subject matter is not registrable under Sections 112 and 113 of the IP Code; (b) subject matter is not new; (c) subject matter extends beyond the content of the application as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation petitions follow prescribed procedures and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial cancellation or restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where grounds for cancellation relate to a part of the industrial design, cancellation may be effected to such extent only; the restriction may be effected as an alteration of the affected features of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may limit cancellation to specific features rather than entire registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of novelty and prior art rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions on 'Novelty' and 'Prior Art' in Part 2, Rules 203, 204 and 204.1 of the Regulations for Patents shall apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty and prior art definitions and tests from patent part apply to designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosure exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of information in the six months preceding filing (industrial design) or twelve months for utility models will not prejudice novelty if disclosure was made by: maker/designer or person with right to registration; a foreign patent office/ Bureau/Office where info was contained in another application filed by the maker that should not have been disclosed; or a third party who obtained info directly/indirectly from the maker/designer. Excludes foreign patent offices that publish pending applications and WIPO PCT publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited categories of prior disclosures are excused from novelty prejudice subject to conditions; consult rules for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to registration and priority claim timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on 'Right to a Patent' apply mutatis mutandis. To claim priority for industrial designs the local application must be filed within six months from the earliest filing date of the corresponding foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claim window for industrial designs is six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of application documents: originals and format
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents to become part of permanent records must be original copies, legibly written/typewritten/printed in permanent ink on one side only. Only certain symbols/formulas not typable may be handwritten. Typing shall be 1½-spaced; capital letters not less than 0.21 cm high and in dark, indelible color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict formatting (originals, ink, spacing, minimum font size) is required for recordability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and physical qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be on A4 (29.7 x 21 cm) paper which shall be pliable, strong, white, smooth, matte, and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified paper quality for all filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line numbering and separate sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract, description and claims must have lines numbered in sets of five restarting each page with numbers on the left margin. Each document (request, description, claims, drawings, abstract) shall commence on a separate sheet and be filed so they can be turned over and joined again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to line numbering and separate-sheet filing conventions for easy examination and file management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and page numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Margins must be: Top 2–4 cm, Left 2.5–4 cm, Right 2–3 cm, Bottom 2–3 cm. Margins must be blank without unnecessary text. Pages of abstract, description and claims shall be numbered consecutively with Arabic numerals appearing in the central portion of either top or bottom margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow precise margin and page numbering specs to avoid formality objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies for voluminous applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract, description, claims, and drawings for voluminous applications shall be filed in two copies if filed manually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide duplicate sets when filing large applications by hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited matter in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must not contain statements contrary to public order or morality; disparaging statements about others' products/processes/patents (mere comparison with prior art not disparaging per se); or matter obviously irrelevant or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will omit prohibited matter at publication and indicate place/number of omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to furnish information on corresponding foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: At the Director's request the applicant shall furnish the date and number of any corresponding foreign application and other documents relating to the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to produce foreign filing details and supporting documents on demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable documents relating to foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: Other documents may include search reports in English prepared by certain Offices, photocopies of relevant documents cited in the search report, copy of the granted patent, copy of examination report or decision on the corresponding foreign application, and other documents facilitating adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide translations as necessary and pertinent search/exam materials to assist Office review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliance with foreign-document requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is considered withdrawn if the applicant fails to furnish requested information concerning the corresponding foreign application within the specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely compliance with Director's requests for foreign documents is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings presentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for formal drawings in Part 4, Rules 413 and 414.1 to 414.15 of the Regulations for Patents apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow patent-part drawing specifications for layout, line weight, symbols, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of attorney or agent recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions on employment of attorney-at-law or agent recommended in Part 4, Rule 421 of the Regulations for Patents apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using counsel or an agent is advised to ensure compliance with formalities and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of resident agent or representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on appointment of resident agent or representative in Part 4, Rules 422 and 422.1 apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-resident applicants must appoint an agent for service in the Philippines as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum and courtesy in conduct of business
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions on decorum and courtesy in the conduct of business in Part 4, Rule 423 apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional behavior in dealings with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply/request registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on who may apply for a patent (Part 5) apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility to apply follows patent-part rules (inventor/assignee/other entitled parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and search procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on 'Classification and Search' in Part 7 of the Regulations for Patents apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs. Unpublished, withdrawn, and forfeited applications will not be cited as references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office classifies and searches as per established patent-part procedures; certain internal documents won't be cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment provisions in Part 9, Rules 916 to 928 of the Regulations for Patents apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant amendments follow analogous patent-part amendment rules (timing, scope, formalities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for response and withdrawal for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on 'Time for Response by Applicant' and 'Withdrawal of Application' in Part 9, Rules 928–930 apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe response deadlines or risk withdrawal; patent-part procedures determine revival and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstitution of application file wrappers
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions on 'Reconstitution of Application File Wrappers' in Part 9, Rule 931 apply mutatis mutandis to utility models or industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules exist for reconstructing lost/damaged file records, following patent-part procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community review notification
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interest of transparency, the concerned community shall be notified by the Office, either through electronic mails or separate notification on the Office website, upon publication of the utility model or industrial design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notification enables third parties to submit adverse information during the publication window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing adverse information by third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month from publication any person may present written adverse information (with required fees) concerning registrability including novelty and industrial applicability while citing relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only adverse information filed in accordance with Regulations will be considered; Office will notify parties of decisions involving such submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and substantiation of adverse information
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse information must be a sworn statement stating the affiant's personal information, circumstances, and grounds for objection and be substantiated by evidence or proof; a registrability report may be attached. Non-compliant submissions will be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse submissions must be formal, sworn, and evidentiary to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference and supplemental adverse information
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party may request a conference at time of filing adverse information by indicating three possible dates within 30 days; Office may request additional information. Within 10 days after the conference parties may file supplemental adverse information in form of sworn statement to include new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference can be used to clarify issues and supplement the adverse submission shortly thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's right to comment on adverse information
rubrics_metrics.description: All adverse information shall be communicated to the applicant who may comment within 30 days from the mailing date of the communication. Copies of adverse information and applicant comments become part of the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants have opportunity to respond and add materials to the file; observe the 30-day comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director decision procedures and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall decide whether to register the utility model or industrial design and may issue a registrability report motu proprio. If prior art defeats registrability the Director may deny registration or direct amendments or supplementation. If Director refuses or denies registration, applicant may appeal to the Director General pursuant to Section 7.1(b) and Part 13; no motion for reconsideration of Director's decision allowed. If Director allows registration, interested parties may file cancellation petitions under specified IP Code sections; appeal to Director General of Director's granting decision is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has broad discretion; appeal routes and limits are specified; cancellation proceedings follow IP Code and inter partes rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration procedure where no adverse information is received
rubrics_metrics.description: If application meets formal requirements and no adverse information is received after the thirty-day publication period, the Director shall decide whether to register the design and may issue a registrability report motu proprio; similar directions to amend or deny apply if prior art defeats registrability. If no defeating prior art exists, Office shall grant registration and inform applicant and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of adverse info does not automatically guarantee registration; Director's registrability assessment may still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and issuance of Certificate of Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate of Registration shall be issued in the name of the Republic of the Philippines under the seal of the Office, signed by the Director, and registered together with the description, claims and drawings in Office records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate formalities are prescribed; registered documents are part of official record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of file contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may inspect the complete description, claims and drawings on file with the Office. Marginal notes and exchanges between applicant and Office shall not be included. Inspection by international IP offices is governed by agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public may review core filed documents subject to agreements; internal correspondence is excluded.
